description: Standalone clamp module promoting std/contracts.mm::clamp into an independent file with extra variants (non-negative clamp, symmetric clamp, saturating clamp). All atoms are fully verifiable with Z3 integer theory. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/math/clamp — verified clamping primitives'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/contracts.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/contracts.mm already use (conditional expressions, comparisons, checked_sub).

atoms.name: clamp_i64
atoms.description: Classic three-way clamp: return min_val when val < min_val, max_val when val > max_val, val otherwise. Mirrors std/contracts.mm::clamp but lives in its own module so downstream code can import only the clamp surface.

atoms.name: clamp_nonneg
atoms.description: Clamp a signed value into [0, max_val]. Negative inputs become 0; oversized inputs become max_val. Common building block for array indices and percent values.

atoms.name: clamp_symmetric
atoms.description: Clamp into the symmetric interval [-bound, bound]. Useful for saturating arithmetic in DSP-style code. Z3 proves the bound directly from two ordered comparisons.

atoms.name: clamp_saturating
atoms.description: Total variant of clamp that tolerates an ill-ordered interval: when min_val > max_val the atom returns min_val instead of rejecting the call. Total function, useful in defensive code paths.
